verdict.reasoning: Patient: "I would say maybe about two months or so, I've been feeling like this" and later notes it has "get worse and worse over the past couple of months," indicating worsening anxiety for ~2 months.

Morning dread: "I just get really nervous every morning about leaving the house"; poor sleep: "I can't get to sleep for hours and hours and hours" and estimates 3-4 hours; palpitations: "I find my heart kind of racing... just a constant like, rapid heart beating."

Onset with new job: "about two months or so... that probably coincides with, me starting a new job"; job is retail head office with difficult boss: "I work for a... fashion retailer, in... the head office team... my boss is not very nice to me"; predominantly work-related: "the majority of it is focused around work as well."

Anticipatory morning anxiety and palpitations: "when I realise in the morning that... I feel like I'm gonna be late" and "I wake up in a panic thinking I am gonna be late"; irregular, minutes to 10 min: Doctor asks if regular/irregular and patient: "Irregular, I think"; "couple of minutes, or... lying there... for like ten minutes."

Doctor: "Any chest pain with that?" Patient: "No, um, well yeah it's painful to , when the heart, when my heart is beating fast but, but, yeah." This reflects no distinct chest pain apart from discomfort when heart is fast.
Low energy and anhedonia: "It's just, really, really low" and "I find no enjoyment at all... anything that, previously was, really fun is just not, it's not enjoyable."

Avoids socializing and exercise: "sometimes... I know that I'm not gonna have fun, because I don't want to, go out" and "I did used to like to like go running... and to play tennis... but now it's just not... I'm not going out to do that quite so much"; no panic attacks: Patient answers about panic attacks: "No I wouldn't say so"; no missed work but thinks of calling in sick: "have you... had to miss work?" Patient: "No" and "pretty much every morning I think, ohh I should call in sick or like, just not go."

Prolonged sleep latency and shallow sleep: "I can't get to sleep for hours and hours" and "even when I'm in sleep it's such a shallow sleep"; wakes before alarm with racing heart: "I do have an alarm, but I find myself waking up before that, 'cause... my heart is racing"; 3–4 hours: "maybe, three, four hours, I'm getting now."

Patient: "No I wouldn't say that I'm eating like, much differently. Ohh that, I probably have more chocolate than normal, just because I feel, so down." This indicates increased chocolate when low but no major appetite change.

Work stress and performance worry: "it's been really stressful" and "really worried about whether I'm doing well or not"; tube rides: "I find public transport really stressful anyway, especially being on the tube it's... really airless."

Low persistent mood even at weekends: "pretty much, down like, I don't enjoy... I'm just so worried" and "even at the weekends... constant, feeling of just being a bit, down"; denies suicidal ideation and has support: "I haven't had any suicidal thoughts" and "I have a good support system, like I do have good family and stuff."

No prior counseling: "I haven't sought any other" (after saying mum recommended GP and no other help); open to one-to-one therapy: Doctor asks if happy to have one-to-one therapy, patient: "Yeah I think, yeah I think so. I've never done that before, but yeah."

Lives with parents: "I live with my parents, just my parents"; drinking pattern: "probably quite a lot on the Friday or Saturday" and "maybe I do have like a bit during the week... maybe a glass of wine during the week"; tobacco occasionally, no illicit drugs: "I try not to smoke, but I do, occasionally, but I don't take drugs."
Patient: "I talk to my mum, because she also suffers from, well she's , suffered from like depression in the past."

Transcript describes generalized anxiety related to work, with insomnia, loss of enjoyment, and daytime low energy, starting about two months coinciding with a stressful new job. These are direct clinical inferences from multiple statements (anxiety, sleep 3–4 h, no enjoyment, low energy, new job 2 months ago).

Doctor assessment: "in terms of palpitations, it is most likely to be a, , associated with anxiety"; episodes are brief (minutes to ~10 minutes) and patient denies distinct chest pain apart from discomfort with fast beats.

Doctor links insomnia to anxiety: "some people, with anxiety they, do need to take medication" and earlier describes anxiety and then addresses sleep; patient clearly attributes difficulty sleeping and shallow sleep to stress/anxiety. Insomnia secondary to anxiety is a direct clinical inference.

Patient: "I probably go over my limit just on those days" (Friday/Saturday) and mentions additional weekday wine, indicating intake above recommended limits; occasional tobacco use confirmed: "I try not to smoke, but I do, occasionally."
Doctor: "you can self-refer via the NHS, for what we call like, talking therapy... So I can send you the link for that." This corresponds to IAPT/CBT self-referral link.
Doctor: "There are some online resources that are really helpful. Um, can put the details, on there and you can, get on with them straight away and try and work through them as well."

Doctor: "if you're feeling like it's not helping at all, or your anxiety is getting worse, to the point where you can't cope with work, or you can't, just do your normal things day-to-day. Then, it's important for us to, for you to give us a call, back and just discuss that, further." This is safety-netting for worsening/functional decline and potential escalation (including panic).
Doctor recommends "couple of basic blood tests" but no specific tests (FBC, U&E, TSH, ferritin, glucose/HbA1c) are named in the transcript. Listing these specific panels is new information.

Transcript: "arranging a GP follow-up a week after you've had the tests" supports timing of follow-up, but there is no mention of considering an ECG or conditions on it. The ECG component is an added detail not in the transcript.

Doctor: "I'll put some more information on your notes about, helping with your, sleep patterns and things like that." No specific advice about regular schedule, reducing late alcohol/caffeine, or wind-down routine is detailed. These specifics are additions.
Although alcohol intake is discussed, the doctor does not explicitly advise reducing it or discuss its impact on anxiety/sleep. Such counseling is not present in the transcript.
While past exercise (running, tennis) is discussed, the doctor does not advise a gradual return to exercise. This recommendation is not mentioned.
Smoking is noted ("I... do, occasionally"), but there is no advice on smoking cessation or offering support resources.

Doctor: "So I can send you the link for that" (talking therapy) and "There are some online resources... can put the details, on there" and "I'll put some more information on your notes" – consistent with sending links/resources via notes/portal.
Doctor: "So if you call the support line you can arrange the, to have the blood test done."

Doctor: "arranging a GP follow-up a week after you've had the tests, so we can just go through the results with you" and earlier safety-net to call back if anxiety worsens, which implies earlier review if deterioration occurs.
